ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, place two strips of paper with parallel opposite sides and equal widths crosswise at will. By rotating one of them, the overlapping part forms a quadrilateral. What can this quadrilateral be?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw heights AE and AF from point D to sides AB and BC, respectively,\\
since quadrilateral ABCD is formed by overlapping two strips of equal width,\\
therefore AB$\parallel$CD, and AD$\parallel$BC,\\
therefore, quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,\\
since DE$\perp$AB, and DF$\perp$BC,\\
therefore DE=DF,\\
since the area of parallelogram ABCD, $S_{\text{parallelogram } ABCD}$=AB$\cdot$DE=BC$\cdot$DF,\\
therefore AB=BC,\\
therefore, quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus.\\
Hence, the answer is: Quadrilateral ABCD is a \boxed{rhombus}.

method.method_draft: First read the figure: the shaded overlap is quadrilateral ABCD; AB and CD lie on one strip's two parallel edges, while AD and BC lie on the other strip's two parallel edges. From the text, the two strips have equal widths. Conclude AB ∥ CD and AD ∥ BC, so ABCD is a parallelogram. The distance between AB and CD is the width of one strip, and the distance between AD and BC is the width of the other strip; these two distances are equal. Use the parallelogram area formula in two ways: area = AB × height to AB = BC × height to BC. Since the two heights are equal, AB = BC. A parallelogram with two adjacent equal sides is a rhombus.

method.method_draft: First read the figure: the overlap is bounded by two pairs of parallel strip edges, giving a parallelogram whose adjacent sides follow the two crossing directions of the strips. From the text, both strip widths are the same, say w. Let the angle between the two strip directions be θ. Moving along one side direction from one boundary of the other strip to its opposite boundary creates a right triangle whose perpendicular width is w and whose hypotenuse is the corresponding side of the overlap; therefore that side length is w/sinθ. The adjacent side is obtained in the same way, crossing the other equal-width strip at the same angle θ, so its length is also w/sinθ. Thus two adjacent sides of the overlap parallelogram are equal, so the quadrilateral is a rhombus.
